title: A Fraction Added Again and Again

steps.body: Adding the same fraction again and again is the simplest kind of fraction multiplication: 2/5 + 2/5 + 2/5 collects three equal groups.
steps.narration: Adding the same fraction again and again is the simplest kind of fraction multiplication: 2/5 + 2/5 + 2/5 collects three equal groups.

widget.prompt: Collect 2/5 three times: build the total on the bar.
widget.successFeedback: 6/5 — three groups of two fifths is six fifths, just past one whole.
widget.lowFeedback: Your shaded bar is shorter than the target half. Shade more — raise the numerator, or use fewer parts.
widget.highFeedback: Your shaded bar is longer than half. Shade less — lower the numerator, or split into more parts.

commonFractions.feedback: 2/5 is a single group. Three of them were collected.
6/10 shrank the pieces as well as counting them; collecting fifths keeps fifths.

predict.reveal: The pieces stay fifths; you simply end up holding six of them instead of two.

cml.actionGoal: Collect equal groups of a fraction and watch only the COUNT of pieces change for g4x repeated.
invariants: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number collects groups of identical pieces: the denominator names the piece size and holds still, while the numerator counts every piece gathered, which is what keeps g4x repeated a counting problem.
misconceptions: Scaling the denominator along with the numerator, adding the whole number to the numerator, or assuming a product cannot pass one whole.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the denominator DID change when you collected groups, what would happen to the size of each piece?

widget.prompt: A hiker walks 1/6 mile, then 3/6 mile more. Express the total as ?/6. What is the numerator?

commonErrors.feedback: 6 names the piece size; joining same-size pieces changes only how MANY there are.
Multiplying the counts is not joining them — 1 pieces and 3 more make 4.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Count the same-size pieces the groups collect; the denominator never changes.

steps.body: Because the pieces are all the same size, joining them is pure counting — the fifths stay fifths, and only how many you hold changes.
steps.narration: Because the pieces are all the same size, joining them is pure counting — the fifths stay fifths, and only how many you hold changes.
